payload.name: Extract one-time events separately from routine activity memories
payload.description: When a user message mentions a specific one-time occurrence (e.g., a sighting, visit, or incident) along with routine or habitual activities, extract the one-time event as its own event memory candidate before updating routine-activity memories.
content: During extraction, identify each distinct event in a message, especially one-time occurrences with explicit or contextual time references (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'on Tuesday').

Create a separate event-memory candidate for each such one-time occurrence, even if the message also describes routine or habitual activities; do not fold the occurrence into an existing routine-activity memory.
When the one-time occurrence and the routine activity share the same topic, still keep the one-time event as an independent memory so it can be retrieved by time or by the event itself.

candidates.solves: This addresses extraction failures where a specific, time-bound occurrence (e.g., seeing wildlife, attending an event) is omitted because the candidate focuses on an accompanying routine activity (e.g., habitual hiking). It applies whenever a message mixes a one-time event with habitual actions; it does not apply when the message only describes routine or recurring activities without a distinct episodic fact.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeTimeEventExtraction
payload.description: When a message mentions a past event or trip with a relative time expression, resolve it using the message timestamp and extract an event memory, even if the mention is casual or incidental.
content: During candidate extraction, identify statements that mention a past location, trip, or event with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last summer', 'yesterday', 'two weeks ago').
Resolve the relative time phrase to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp (e.g., 'last summer' in a message from early 2023 means summer 2022).
Extract an event memory (type 'event') capturing the person, location/activity, and resolved absolute time, even if the mention is incidental or appears in a casual message.

candidates.solves: The construction agent failed to persist a past event mentioned with a relative time phrase in a casual message, leaving the fact missing. This Skill instructs extracting event memories for any past trips or events mentioned, resolving relative time to absolute time from the session timestamp, even when the mention is incidental.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Duration Relationships
payload.description: When a message states how long a relationship or recurring activity lasted (e.g., 'for X years', 'since 2019'), extract it as a relationship/event candidate even if the utterance is conversational and not a direct answer.
content: During extraction, treat explicit duration phrases attached to relationships, memberships, or repeated activities as mandatory candidate triggers. Capture the actor, the relationship/activity, and the duration. Do not skip a candidate merely because the sentence also contains social small talk.

When applying CRUD, before adding a new memory, check whether the existing memory pool already stores the same relationship/activity without a duration; if so, propose an UPDATE to add the duration rather than creating a duplicate relationship record.
Do not infer durations from vague wording such as 'for a while' or 'long time'; only trigger on explicit time spans or clear starting points like 'since 2019' or 'for X years'.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: a conversational turn with an explicit duration phrase for a relationship produced no extraction candidate, so the duration and relationship were never stored. Reusable mechanism: extraction can miss explicit duration signals when they are embedded in casual speech. This applies to any future message stating how long a relationship, membership, or recurring activity lasted, whether or not it answers a direct question.

payload.name: Preserve Event Time in Extraction
payload.description: When a user reports a one-time action or change with a time cue ('recently', 'last weekend', explicit dates), during extraction store it as an event memory with the resolved concrete date in the content, not as a time-less profile enrichment.
content: During extraction, when a statement describes a one-time action or change (joined, started, bought, moved, etc.) with a time cue, resolve the time from the message/session timestamp and create an 'event' memory that includes both the action and the concrete date (e.g., 'joined X on 2023-11-04').

Do not merge such time-anchored events into a profile or state memory without the event date; if updating an existing memory, include the resolved date in the content so time-anchored queries can retrieve it.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates often collapse time-anchored events (e.g., 'recently joined a group') into static profile states, dropping the event date, which makes later time-anchored queries fail. This rule preserves the resolved absolute time and event nature, and applies to any one-time action with a relative or explicit time cue in future sessions.

payload.name: ExtractCompletedTaskEvents
payload.description: When a user states they finished or completed a project or task, extract an event memory with the project/task detail and resolved time reference.
content: During candidate extraction, create an event candidate whenever a participant explicitly states they completed, finished, or wrapped up a project or task. Include the participant as the subject, the project/task description, and the resolved time (e.g., 'last week' relative to the message timestamp).
Do not skip such statements because they appear in a casual or conversational reply; the fact is still durable and should be stored.

candidates.solves: The construction pipeline missed a user's self-reported completion of a project because the statement was embedded in a conversational reply and no candidate was created. This skill enforces extraction of explicit 'completed X' statements as event memories, applicable to any future message where a participant mentions finishing a task or project, regardless of conversational framing.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeTimePastLocations
payload.description: When a message mentions a past vacation, trip, or visit with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last summer', 'last year'), resolve the time against the message timestamp and extract the person's location as an event/state memory during ingestion.
content: During extraction, when a message describes a past trip, vacation, or visit with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last summer', 'last year', 'a few months ago'), resolve the phrase against the message/session timestamp and create an event or state memory for the person being in the named location during that resolved period.
If the message names only a city or region, include its country in the location value when the country is unambiguous; otherwise record only the explicit location.
Do not defer this extraction: create the memory at ingestion time from the evidence available in the message.

candidates.solves: Construction failed because a temporally qualified location was expressed with a relative time phrase and only a city name, so no candidate was generated. The abstract mechanism is missing extraction of location facts that require resolving relative time references against the message timestamp and inferring an unambiguous country. This rule applies to any future session where a person states where they were during a past period using relative time language, and ensures such facts are stored at ingestion time.

payload.name: Inherit established location in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from a message that omits a location, check earlier messages in the same session for an established location and include it if the event clearly occurs there.
content: Before creating an event memory, review earlier messages in the current session for a location already associated with the speaker's current trip or ongoing activities.
If the message describes an event within that established location, include the location in the extracted memory content even if the current message does not name it.
Do not add a location from earlier context when the event is not plausibly tied to it or when the earlier location is no longer current.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes extract an event memory from a message while dropping the location established earlier in the same conversation, so later questions about where the event happened cannot be answered. This rule makes extraction context-aware by carrying forward a location already tied to the speaker's current trip or activities, and it applies whenever a future message describes an event without repeating a location the session has already established.

payload.name: Extract event memories from casual first-person statements
payload.description: When a user states a personal past action or experience with a relative time reference (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday'), extract it as an event memory, even if the statement is embedded in a question or casual conversation.
content: During candidate extraction, identify explicit statements of personal past actions or experiences that include a time reference. Resolve relative times (e.g., 'last Friday') to concrete dates using the message/session timestamp and create an `event` memory with the resolved date and action. Do not skip such statements because the message also asks a question, or because the action seems incidental.

candidates.solves: Messages often contain first-person past actions with relative time references (e.g., 'last Friday I made X') that are easily overlooked when the message also asks a question or discusses a topic. The diagnosed failure shows no candidate was generated for such a statement, so the fact was lost. A general rule to extract these explicit events, resolving the date from the session timestamp, prevents this omission across any topic or entity. This rule does not apply to opinions, preferences, or hypothetical statements without a specific past time reference.

payload.name: Preserve_relative_time_wording
payload.description: During extraction or CRUD review, if a source statement contains a relative time expression (e.g., 'a few years ago', 'last week'), preserve its exact wording in the memory content; do not substitute a semantic variant.
content: During extraction, when creating a memory candidate from a statement that includes a relative time expression (e.g., 'a few years ago', 'recently', 'last month'), use that exact phrase in the candidate content; do not change it to a different quantifier ('several'), a vaguer term ('sometime ago'), or an absolute date unless the source explicitly equates them.
During CRUD, if an existing memory's relative time expression conflicts with the source statement, update the memory to the source's exact wording.

candidates.solves: A diagnosed failure showed an extraction candidate paraphrased 'a few years ago' as 'several years ago', changing the answer to a later question about event timing. The mechanism is semantic drift of relative time qualifiers during paraphrase-based memory construction. Preserving exact temporal wording transfers to any event memory that answers 'when' questions (purchases, visits, milestones, etc.) and is bounded to relative time expressions; absolute dates can be recorded directly when the source gives them.

payload.name: Preserve explicit event timing in memory extraction
payload.description: When constructing an event memory from a message that states when it occurred, keep that explicit time (e.g., 'a year ago', 'last week', 'in 2023') in the memory content or world_start.
content: When extracting or updating an event memory, if the source message includes an explicit time expression for the event, preserve it by adding the expression to the memory content or setting world_start from the message timestamp; do not omit it when summarizing the event.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction summarized 'I bought it a year ago in Paris' into a general acquisition memory without the temporal modifier, so later the purchase time was unknowable. The failure mechanism is dropping explicit event timing while compressing source details into memory. This Skill applies to any future construction turn where a stated event time (relative or absolute) is present, across topics such as purchases, life events, or ownership changes.

payload.name: Resolve-relative-dates-and-preserve-event-qualifiers
payload.description: When a message contains a relative date (yesterday, today, last week) or an ordinal qualifier (first time), resolve the absolute date and preserve all event details when extracting or updating memories.
content: During extraction, resolve relative time expressions (e.g., 'yesterday', 'today', 'last week') to absolute dates using the message/session timestamp; write the resolved date in the memory content and event start field.
When source text includes qualifiers like 'first time', 'only', or a specific location, keep them in the memory; do not replace temporarily anchored facts with vague summaries such as 'recently'.
Before ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, verify that any memory for a dated or one-time event contains an explicit date; if the date or qualifier is missing from the candidate, fix the extraction or issue an update.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often drops exact dates and qualifiers when messages use relative time ('yesterday') or ordinals ('first time'), leaving memories unable to answer 'when did X first...' queries. This skill enforces relative-date resolution from the message timestamp and preservation of ordinal/location details, making future dated-event memories answerable. Applies to specific dated events during extraction, not to routine summaries without a temporal anchor.

payload.name: Extract explicit dated family events from nostalgic messages
payload.description: When a user shares a personal or family event with a specific year/date in a nostalgic or emotional message, generate an event memory candidate during extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, if a message contains an explicit statement about a personal or family event with a time reference (e.g., 'my parents' wedding in 1993'), create an event memory candidate even when the message is framed as a memory, photo caption, or emotional reflection.
Use the appropriate memory kind (event) and include the relationship and date as stated. Do not discard facts because the tone is nostalgic or the evidence is a photo.

candidates.solves: This solves missed event extraction when explicit dated facts are embedded in nostalgic or photo-caption messages. The diagnosis showed a message stating 'my parents' wedding in 1993' produced no candidates. The rule abstracts the mechanism: construction agents may under-extract explicit facts in reflective context. It applies to any future message where a user mentions a dated personal/family event in a reminiscing tone.

payload.name: Extract illustrative personal events with resolved dates
payload.description: When processing a message for memory construction, if the speaker states a personal event or activity as an example, aside, or illustration, use this Skill to capture it as a distinct fact and resolve any relative time expression from the message timestamp.
content: Treat every directly stated speaker event as a separate extraction candidate, even when the message's main purpose is encouragement, advice, or opinion.
Resolve relative time expressions (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday', 'this morning') using the message/session timestamp and set the event's start time accordingly.
Do not fold a distinct personal event into a memory that only summarizes the speaker's attitude or ongoing support; keep the event available as its own queryable memory.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often summarizes a message's dominant conversational intent (e.g., encouragement or advice) and drops a directly stated personal event that the speaker mentions as an example or aside. Future questions can target that dropped event, so no memory supports it. This Skill instructs extractors to preserve every directly stated speaker event as its own fact and to resolve relative time expressions from the message/session timestamp, making such events queryable across equivalent future conversations.

payload.name: ExtractEventsWithRelativeTime
payload.description: When a speaker mentions a past event using relative time (e.g., last year, last summer, two months ago), extract it as an event memory during candidate extraction and resolve the date from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, treat deictic time phrases (last year, last summer, two weeks ago, etc.) as sufficient evidence of a past event. Resolve them against the message or session timestamp to an explicit date (e.g., year/month) and emit an `event` candidate if the statement describes a real-world occurrence such as a trip, visit, project, or milestone.
Do not skip a fact solely because no absolute date is written; convert the relative time and include the resolved date in the memory.
If the exact calendar unit cannot be determined, record the best approximation and keep the original phrase in the evidence/source link.

candidates.solves: Construction often omits facts stated with relative time ('last year') when no absolute date appears, leaving events unextracted. This skill instructs the extraction stage to treat such deictic references as event triggers, resolve them against the message timestamp, and create dated event memories. Applies to conversational statements about trips, visits, or milestones using relative time; not for CRUD merging or fully explicit dates.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeEventDates
payload.description: When extracting or updating an event memory from a message containing a relative time expression (yesterday, today, last week), resolve it to an absolute date using the message timestamp and store that date in the memory.
content: During extraction, if the source message contains a relative time expression (e.g., yesterday, today, last week), convert it to an absolute date using the message's occurred_at timestamp; for example, 'yesterday' refers to the day before the message date.

Store the resolved absolute date in the candidate content and set world_start to that date (not the message date) for event memories; when enriching an existing event memory via UPDATE, preserve or add the resolved date.

candidates.solves: During construction, event facts mentioned with relative time references (e.g., 'yesterday') are often stored without the resolved absolute date, causing later date-based queries to fail. This skill applies whenever extraction or an update processes a message containing relative time expressions: resolve them to absolute dates using the message timestamp and store the resolved date in the memory. It does not apply to explicitly stated calendar dates, which should be stored as given.

operations.name: Extract Dated Event Memories
operations.description: Use when a message states a one-time or past event with a time reference, even if casual or incidental.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement of a one-time or past event (trip, visit, completion, purchase, family event, etc.) as a candidate, even if the message is casual, nostalgic, or includes routine activities.

Resolve relative time expressions (e.g., 'yesterday', 'last week', 'last summer') to absolute dates using the message/session timestamp and store the resolved date in the memory content and world_start.
Preserve explicit time qualifiers and event details (e.g., 'first time', location, duration) in the memory; do not drop them when summarizing.
When a message omits a location but earlier in the session a location is established for the speaker's current activities, include that location in the event memory if the event clearly occurs there.
Do not fold a distinct event into a routine-activity or profile memory; keep it as its own event memory.
operations.reason: All candidates share the same underlying mechanism: extraction of time-anchored event memories with relative time resolution and preservation of event details.
